summary: Quenched and tempered (Q&T) cast SAE 4130 Cr–Mo steel, included in Bartlett and Van Aken's review as the reference benchmark against which the strength and dynamic fracture toughness of Fe–30Mn–9Al–0.9C lightweight austenitic steels are compared.
composition: The paper does not report the actual chemical composition of this benchmark; Table IV identifies it only as "Cast 4130" with the heat treatment "Quenched and tempered". SAE 4130 is conventionally a chromium–molybdenum low-alloy steel, and the review consistently refers to the benchmark family as "quenched and tempered Cr-Mo steels (SAE 4130)", used as a density and property reference for the lightweight Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys.
processing: The alloy is in the cast condition and was quenched and tempered (Q&T). Specific austenitizing temperature, quench medium, tempering temperature/time, and cooling media are not reported in the paper.
properties: Dynamic fracture toughness (DFT) was determined by the Schindler single-specimen technique from instrumented Charpy impact tests on fatigue-precracked Charpy specimens, following ASTM E 1820 and ASTM E 813. Two quenched-and-tempered conditions are reported for this benchmark: a 350 BHN condition with a DFT of 94 kJ/m² and a 330 BHN condition with a DFT of 136 kJ/m². The softer Q&T condition thus exhibits the higher dynamic fracture toughness.
mechanisms: Porosity in high-strength quenched and tempered Cr–Mo steel was reported to decrease notch toughness by more than 50 kJ/m², indicating that casting soundness (micro-porosity) is a key microstructural control on the toughness of the cast 4130 benchmark.

In the two reported Q&T conditions of cast 4130, lowering the hardness from 350 BHN to 330 BHN is accompanied by an increase in dynamic fracture toughness from 94 kJ/m² to 136 kJ/m², reflecting the conventional strength–toughness trade-off in quenched and tempered steels.
conclusions: The quenched and tempered cast SAE 4130 serves as the benchmark alloy for correlating strength and dynamic fracture toughness with the Fe–30Mn–9Al–0.9C lightweight steels. The fully austenitic Fe–30Mn–9Al–0.9C cast steels are almost 15% less dense than quenched and tempered Cr–Mo steels (SAE 4130) while offering equivalent strengths and dynamic fracture toughness, and in some conditions considerably higher dynamic fracture toughness, supporting their potential for transportation lightweighting and improved crashworthiness.
